baseline_protocol: two unconditional GETs versus first GET then If-None-Match GET; ETag covers entire serialized response envelope
limitations: Both input observations are genuine saved publisher snapshots but the GETs, responses, task, headers and ETag server behavior are constructed, not observed.
This does not establish whether the x402 List origin implements ETag, HTTP caching, 304, or cache freshness.
The two rolling 30-day settlement windows overlap; they are not incremental verified sales.
ETag 304 still requires revalidation and does not eliminate an origin request in this modeled direct-to-origin design.
No HTTP transport compression, TLS, TCP, hosting, cache storage, memory, tokens or paid buyer activity was measured.
The earlier retained-base result is canonical JSON and cannot be directly compared numerically with these modeled HTTP/1.1 frames.
decision: Standard conditional GET is an essential free baseline for identical data; it cannot substitute for delta delivery on changed responses, but modeled HTTP savings do not establish a differentiated monetizable product. Prioritize real buyer tasks and measured full unit economics before deployment.
